d.title: Which algorithms care about scale, and why
d.caption: The reason is always the same shape: something in the objective sums across features with one coefficient. A distance adds squared differences; one λ penalises every weight equally; one learning rate steps every input. A tree compares one feature with one constant and never adds anything across columns — so any monotone rescaling gives identical splits.
cells: the widest column dominates the distance
one lambda penalises every weight equally
one step size for every input
the optimum is unit-free; conditioning is not
a split is one feature against a constant
each feature is modelled on its own

d.title: Three scalers, and what an outlier does to each
d.caption: The choice is about which statistic the outlier can move. Min-max is defined by the extremes, so a single bad value compresses every other row into a corner; robust scaling uses the median and IQR, which an outlier cannot shift. And a scaler that centres destroys sparsity — which is why `with_mean=False` exists.
cells: compresses all other rows into a corner

d.title: Seven encodings, by what each one assumes
d.caption: The assumption column is the whole decision. Ordinal encoding asserts an order, so applying it to an unordered column hands the model a ranking you invented — usually alphabetical, because that is what the encoder saw first. Target encoding assumes a level's mean outcome is informative, and leaks unless it is fitted in-fold.

d.title: Two thousand cities: what one-hot costs and what replaces it
d.caption: At high cardinality one-hot is not merely wide — most columns have too few ones to estimate anything from, so the model is fitting noise in two thousand places. Each alternative collapses the column to one or a few, and each pays for it differently.

d.title: The mechanism decides what is safe to do
d.caption: Under MNAR the value's own size is what caused it to be absent — high earners declining to state income — so every imputer fills in a typical value for rows that are systematically atypical. No imputation recovers the values; an indicator column recovers the **fact**, which is often the stronger feature.
cells: impute from them, plus an indicator
indicator first; no imputer recovers it

d.title: Row deletion scored best and would have been the worst decision
d.caption: The 126 customers with no tickets field churn at 0.222 against 0.154 — dropping them raised the AUC because the **remaining problem is easier**, not because the model improved. The deployed model meets those customers on day one, with no tickets value, and still has to score them. A treatment is judged on the population the model will serve.
cells: it recovers the fact, not the value
it compounds and empties the table
the fills would be mostly fiction
it learns a direction per split

d.title: Nine shapes of derived feature, and who needs them
d.caption: The last column is the part worth internalising: most of these exist to give a **linear or distance** model something it cannot construct itself. A tree can already find a threshold interaction by nesting two splits, so generic polynomial expansion mostly adds width and noise there.
cells: sin and cos of the part

d.title: Find, then decide — and they are separate steps
d.caption: Detection is a statistical question with several answers; what to do about it is a domain question with only one source of truth. Collapsing them is how a genuine extreme value — the bulk order, the record day — gets winsorised into a plausible-looking lie.

d.title: What each selector can and cannot see
d.caption: The two columns that decide most choices: whether the test can see a **non-linear** relationship at all, and what it does with correlated copies. An F-test ranks every copy of a useful feature highly; lasso picks one of them arbitrarily; permutation importance shares the credit, so a correlated copy can hide the drop entirely.

d.title: Where selection must run
d.caption: Selecting on all the rows means the choice of columns was informed by the rows you later score — and with more features than rows you can select pure noise and get a convincing cross-validated number out of it. The selector is a fitted step like any other.

d.title: The contract every transformer keeps
d.caption: Three methods and one rule: nothing is learned until `fit`, and everything learned is stored in an attribute ending in an underscore. Before `fit`, a scaler has no such attributes at all — which is exactly why a pipeline can be cloned per fold and refitted without leaking anything between them.

d.title: One artefact, one code path
d.caption: Training–serving skew is not a risk you manage, it is a consequence of having two implementations. If the fitted Pipeline is the thing serialised and the thing called in serving, there is no second implementation to drift.
